tools.name: windows_list
tools.title: List windows

tools.name: schema
tools.title: Read a request’s schema
tools.description: Read the request schema for one operation, exports.run or themes.edit, with only its referenced definitions. Use it before proposals_create for each operation you send, and themes.edit before themes_edit. Omit selector for the complete proposal schema. With detail: "fields", it lists the request’s fields in place of its schema: each one’s type, whether every request needs it, its values when the schema names them, and its description. Without a selector, it lists the proposal request’s own fields, then each operation’s name and the fields it always needs. This only reads the contract; it never proposes or edits. It needs no open presentation.

detail.description: `fields` answers with an index of the request's fields in place of its schema.

selector.description: One operation's name, exports.run or themes.edit; omitted, the complete proposal request.

tools.name: presentations_get
tools.title: Read the presentation
tools.description: Current issues, revision, slide ids, the presentation’s own properties as updatePresentationProperties sets them (footer, date, locale, default transition, soundtrack, self-playing) the slides and sections in order (outline), and the accepted theme catalog: layout keys and their placeholders, schemes and text styles. Use those keys when inserting or changing slides. Each issue has a severity: error or warning. Its disposition says what the app does about it: show-presentation, skip-object, refuse-slide or refuse-presentation. Warnings with code text-overflow name each object whose words run past its frame on a slide as its steps leave it, where they still show (slides_render’s fittedFrames give the frame that holds them); text-hidden names each object some of whose words the slide’s edge, the end of their path or their table cell hides, which an export asks about; and text-overflow-unchecked says that could not be measured. It reads the files first: when they cannot be taken in, as after a hand edit the parser refuses, `stalled` gives the reason and the parser errors, and the rest describes the presentation as last read.

tools.name: slides_get
tools.title: Read a slide
tools.description: Read one slide at authored Base or an exact moment of its motion: its objects as the .mdpoint file spells them, each with its words as text when it holds any (exactly what setText takes), its notes, drawnFrames and drawnEnds: where each is drawn, as transformObjects takes it, which theme level owns each, authored initial values/steps, playbackStepIds in presenter advance order, parameter targets with current values and interpolation, and revision. Dormant steps remain authored for repair but do not consume advances. Slide ids come from presentations_get and slides_get results and the .mdpoint file, never ordinals. A read never starts media.

animationValueSchemas.description: Each parameter's value domain by object type, then by parameter, once for each type on the slide that has it: a type holds its own range where it differs, as a text's scale and a model's do. A dry run still checks each value against its own object.

default-step-duration.description: The master's default-step-duration, or the format's default, in seconds: the length a new step's fades and moves take and its min-duration, and the length a by-paragraph delivery starts with.

drawnEnds.description: Where each line's ends are drawn as authored, whatever `moment` names, by id: a free end where auto layout places it, an end on an object where it meets that object.

drawnFrames.description: Where each object a transform moves by a frame is drawn as authored, whatever `moment` names, by id: the frame transformObjects' `drawnFrame` takes and gives back, in the same space, its turn and scale apart. A growing text box stands at the size its words take, a table at its rows' height, a group at the box its members give it, an object auto layout places where it places it. A travel's `drawnPoints` are where this frame's corner goes.

moment.description: Null is Base. A sampled moment reports the actual clamped time; Start has null stepId and time zero.

notes.description: The slide's speaker notes, their whole Markdown exactly as replaceText compares its `before` with them when its `objectId` is null, from the same revision; null when the slide has none, as setNotes clears them.

objects.description: The slide's objects as authored, before any animation, whatever `moment` names: groups and each object's parent included, with the ids an edit names, each as the .mdpoint file spells it, a growing text's `frame` the point its growth holds, and an object auto layout places where its file stores it; the values at the `moment` are each target's `animationParameters` value.

playbackStepIds.description: Ordered steps that consume presenter advances. Dormant authored steps remain in steps for editing.

fileScopes.description: Whose folder each file an object names is in, by the key that names it; a key the object doesn't hold is absent.

provenance.description: Which theme level owns each object. AgentSlideObject.description: An object as the .mdpoint file spells it, with its words when it holds text (a text box, a shape, a table, a chart): exactly the Markdown setText takes, so writing it back unchanged changes nothing; "" for empty words. A paragraph's `<!-- id: … -->` at the end of its last line is the id a step's text cue names it by, and it travels with its paragraph. In words written without ids, an unchanged paragraph keeps its id wherever it moves. Every other paragraph keeps its id where its words start: a split's first part keeps it, and a join keeps the first paragraph's. Give a new paragraph none, so the app gives it one and its own step. Words that leave out a paragraph a step's cue names are refused, naming the step: keep the paragraph's id, or remove the cue first.

PresentationAnimationBounceInterpolation.description: A bounce at a bounciness, Blender's Rigid Body word for a rebound's share of the speed it lands with; Blender's Bounce at 0.5.

PresentationAnimationCubicBezier.description: A cubic Bézier as the files hold it: its handles at (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), named as CSS's cubic-bezier() names its four numbers.

PresentationAnimationCurveSource.description: A curve as the file spells it: its keyframes, its loop's word and the keyframe that loop starts from, the first when it names none.

PresentationAnimationElasticInterpolatio.description: Blender's Elastic ringing into its keyframe: its ring as a multiple of the move, and its length in seconds, or 0.3 of the move.

exponential-scale.description: Whether the move to this keyframe scales at an even rate, as After Effects' Exponential Scale does.

id.description: Caller-minted stable ID; new keyframes/cues share one unique namespace within the step. Reusing an ID replaces the whole event.

interpolation.description: Interpolation into this keyframe, from the preceding keyframe or the step's start.

end.description: When it would have ended, in step seconds, at or after the keyframe's time; it does not extend the step.

interrupted.description: The longer move this keyframe interrupts: up to this keyframe, the motion follows that move's curve.

oscillate.description: An oscillation added from this keyframe on, its wave named as the file names it.

path.description: On a point keyframe, `frame.xy`, `translation.xy` or `position.xyz`: the move into it bends along this path.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

value.description: Null clears an optional property; its current text-style/default then applies.

PresentationAnimationKeyframeSource.description: A keyframe as the file spells it: a move's `end` and `exponential-scale`, and a fill as the object spells its fill.

frequency.description: Cycles a second, as After Effects' wiggle() frequency sets it; a noise wanders at that rate.

phase.description: Degrees into the cycle at the keyframe.

seed.description: Which noise a noise wave draws, as Motion's Random Seed picks one; the same seed always draws the same.

PresentationAnimationOscillationSource.description: An oscillation as the file spells it: its wave is `wave-shape`.

anyOf.description: A geometry parameter as the file names it: a line's ends are its start and end.

PresentationAnimationParameterSource.description: A parameter as the file names it: `stroke-weight`, `crop.focal-point.x`, `frame.x`.

orient.description: Turn the object to face along the path as it moves.

PresentationAnimationPath.description: A path in the move's own frame: the start is 0 0, the end 1 0, and y a quarter turn clockwise from x, as SVG's.

PresentationAnimationPoint.description: A point keyframe's value: a frame's or a translation's x and y, or a 3D position's x, y and z.

PresentationAnimationSpring.description: A spring landing on its keyframe: `amount` sets how far it swings past, from 0, which settles with no overshoot, to 1, and `response` its period in seconds as SwiftUI's does, or it fits the keyframe.

PresentationAnimationTargetSource.description: A curve's target as the file names it: its object's id is `object`.

anyOf.description: What a keyframe holds: a number, a flag, a color or a role, a fill, lengths, a shadow, a 3D object's whole orientation, or a point.

PresentationAnimationValueSource.description: A value as the file spells it: a fill as `accent` or a gradient whose stops name their colors.

id.description: Who they are: `local:` and a lowercase UUID for a computer's user, `shared:` and 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits for a collaboration service member, or `dropbox:` and a Dropbox account id; absent when the writer knows none.

name.description: The name they wrote it under.

PresentationCommentPosition.description: Fractions of the slide's width and height, independent of its current size.

color.description: A color role or an opaque CSS hex: a role's own opacity doesn't reach the shadow, whose opacity is its only one.

offset.description: Across and down from the object, in the object's own turn.

size.description: How far past what casts it the shadow reaches, as Photoshop's Size.

spread.description: The share of the size, 0–1, by which what casts the shadow grows solid before the rest of the size blurs, as Photoshop's Spread: at 1 the shadow stands solid all the way out. None where left out.

PresentationDropShadow.description: A drop shadow, as Photoshop's Layer Style › Drop Shadow sets one: how far it reaches, how much of that reach stands solid, how far each way it falls and in what color. Its lengths are canvas units, and a text's are ems of its size.

PresentationObjectLevel.description: Where an object the slide shows, its own or inherited, came from, and which of its properties the slide overrides.

PresentationOrientation.description: A 3D object's orientation in quaternion mode, whole, its w with x, y and z: a quaternion of length 1.

PresentationStepCueSource.description: What a cue starts, as the file spells it: its `type`, and a clip's `clip-trim`, `blend-in` and `clip-scale`.

min-duration.description: The least seconds the step lasts; left out or 0, it lasts as long as what it holds.

repeat-count.description: Play the step this many times before it completes; omitted plays once.

start.description: Plays without a click of its own: with the step before it, or after that step ends, as PowerPoint's With Previous and After Previous do. Its times then count from that start. On the first step it plays after the transition. Omitted, the step waits for a click.

PresentationStepSource.description: A step as its file writes it.

RenderFileScope.description: Whose folder a file is in: the presentation's, its theme's, or the cache where MarkdownPoint keeps the models it builds from a text's letters on this computer.

end.description: The file's or the Action's end when absent.

model-node-name.description: the name of one of the model’s nodes

opaque-color.description: a color role or a hex color without opacity, such as "#000000"

tools.name: slides_render
tools.title: Render a slide
tools.description: Render one slide through the app renderer at authored Base or an exact moment of its motion. Base is the slide as authored, before any animation; Start applies initial values. Returns a PNG image plus revision, the moment as MarkdownPoint spells it, its width and height in pixels, and overflowing: the objects whose text does not fit their frames there, as the canvas marks them, fittedFrames: the frame each text object takes fitted to its text there, in its own parameters, its height as Fit box to text fits it and its width with every paragraph on one line as a side handle fits it, its letters kept where they stand, to write as transformObjects’ drawnFrame at the same moment, and textBounds: where each object's words stand there in canvas units, the union of its lines' boxes. It never starts media or changes the presentation.

longestEdge.description: Maximum PNG edge in pixels, preserving the slide's aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024.

anyOf.description: A step's stable id, as `slides.get` lists it.

time.description: Seconds within the step, at least 0; 0 at Start.

output.description: Absolute path of a new .png file outside any presentation folder, which the app writes instead of returning the image inline; the result then names it in files and carries no image.

slideId.description: A slide's stable id, as presentations.get and slides.get list it.

view.description: slide (the default) as the audience sees it; top or left for the slide's 3D content from above, the audience at the bottom, or from the slide's left, the audience on the right, with the slide's plane and its shadow catchers' planes drawn in and lines from the slide's corners toward its camera, to judge depth a front view hides. A slide with no 3D content has no top or side view.

presentation.description: The presentation folder to target (from windows_list). Omit to use the focused window, or the only open presentation when none is focused.

tools.name: slides_frames
tools.title: Render animation frames
tools.description: Render one animation step over a range of its time, or with transition: true the slide’s transition into the next shown slide (Carry over included) over its duration, sampled at a rate, through the app renderer: returns a contact sheet of every frame, each labeled with its time, plus the times and frame size. With output, the app also writes frame-0001.png onward and sheet.png into that absolute directory. At most 120 frames; lower fps or narrow from/to for longer steps. It never starts media or changes the presentation.

fps.description: Frames a second it samples, 30 when omitted.

from.description: Seconds within the step where the range starts. Defaults to 0.

longestEdge.description: Maximum frame edge in pixels, preserving the slide's aspect ratio. Defaults to 512.

output.description: A new or empty folder outside any presentation folder, which the frames are written into as frame-0001.png onward beside sheet.png; the result names them in files. Omitted, only the sheet returns.

slideId.description: A slide's stable id, as presentations.get and slides.get list it.

tools.name: slides_measure
tools.title: Measure a slide’s 3D content
tools.description: Measure a step’s 3D content over a range of its time, or with waits: true the slide at every wait for a click its show makes, from the geometry the page samples. For each model and 3D text at each time: its bounds on the slide and its shadows’, how much of each text’s box its silhouette and its shadow cover, and how far its lowest point stands above the slide’s floor, its highest floor object. A model covers flat words where its silhouette falls on their box through the camera, whichever of them draws in front, and 3D words only where it draws in front of their letters. A shadow covers a text where it falls on its box. A shadow here is the sharp outline its parts cast on each catcher. A render shows what is seen. Over the range: for a model with an in-place walk, how fast its planted feet slide against its body’s travel, and the speed each walk travels at its size, at which its feet hold; and for each text, the most it is covered and shadowed, and when. Numbers decide what a picture misjudges: a model landing beside words, feet sliding, a shadow over a headline. With waits: true in place of stepId and a range: the slide at every wait for a click its show makes, where it holds until the next click. That is as it has appeared when its first click waits, after each click once that click’s steps, their with and after members, its Actions and the camera’s drift have ended, and after the last. A wait that loops is measured over one period, fps times a second, 30 when omitted: its 3D’s loop, or its 2D’s while the 3D stands still; where both loop at lengths of their own, the 2D on its own clock over the 3D’s period. A wait where the show holds the 3D still while something in it would move on gives its hold, the cause and the objects to change, as the slide’s warning does: fix it, or the show freezes the 3D there. Each sample adds how much of each object draws, 0 to 1, its opacity and its groups’, 0 while hidden; and for each text, the most a drawn model covers it while it draws, and at which wait. At most 120 samples. Nothing changes.

The call waits for the existing app export to finish and returns its report, whose files names every file written; there are no durable jobs or automatic retries. Export does not alter the authored presentation. When words are hidden, by a slide’s edge, the end of a path or a table cell, the refusal is { code: "refused", message }. Its message names the slides. Resend with a fresh id and confirmHiddenText: true only when the hidden words are acceptable. tools.description: Copy an image, video, audio file or 3D model into the presentation’s folder, as the app’s media picker does, and return the file’s path in the presentation, which insertObject and replaceMedia take. An image also returns its size, its pixels as saved: a PNG, JPEG or WebP longer than 4096 pixels on a side is saved at 4096 on its long side, in its own type, and reducedFrom gives the pixels it had. An animated one, one too large to reduce and every other type are saved whole. Give path for a file on this machine, or name (with the media’s extension) and data (its bytes in base64) when the file is not reachable. A movie takes its first frame as its poster; when that frame cannot be read it is still imported and warnings says so. A model (.glb, or a .gltf by path with its files beside it) becomes one self-contained GLB: compressed geometry and KTX2 textures decoded, its own cameras and lights removed, its Actions named apart; changes says what changed and report what the model does, as models_inspect gives it. tools.name: models_build
tools.title: Build a 3D model
tools.description: Build a 3D model from code and save it as media/<name>-<hash>.glb, a file a model object can show. source is an ES module whose default export build(kit, data) returns { model, actions }: a three.js Object3D in glTF meters, +Y up, facing +Z, its origin where it stands (a character’s feet), and its AnimationClips. kit holds THREE, GLTFExporter, GLTFLoader, SVGLoader, FontLoader, TextGeometry, ConvexGeometry, ParametricGeometry, RoundedBoxGeometry, BufferGeometryUtils, SkeletonUtils, SimplifyModifier, TessellateModifier and MeshSurfaceSampler; model(file), which loads a model of the presentation named in models; and separate(mesh), which splits a mesh by the pieces no edge joins, for an Action to turn or move each: the mesh keeps its largest piece and its origin, and each other piece becomes a mesh beside it, its origin at its own bounds center, which separate returns. A material named color:<role> takes the slide’s color of that role. userData { markdownpoint: { "cast-shadow": false } } on an object, or { markdownpoint: { loop: true } } on an AnimationClip, which becomes an Action, become its extras. It runs in a sandbox with no network or files, for at most 60 s. The model is imported as a file is: lights and cameras removed, Actions named apart. The source runs only while it builds. No file keeps it. To change a model you built, build it again from new source. Returns the file, changes, the report models_inspect gives, and a sheet: the saved model from eight sides, top and side, and each Action at four times. To build a text object’s words, give slideId and textId: data.words then holds its letters as its slide lays them out, which kit.text(data.words, { depth, bevel }) extrudes into { model, letters }, one node per letter, one model unit an em of the text’s size, the origin on its first baseline at the left of its column, saved as generated/<name>-<hash>.glb: a text’s model is MarkdownPoint’s, not one of the author’s media. Plain 3D letters need no build: a text’s model { extrusion: { depth, bevel } }, which MarkdownPoint builds. The answer adds built-from: set the text’s model to { file: the answer’s file, "built-from": its built-from } with updateObjectProperties, and the slide draws the model while the words are the ones built; once the words or font change, it draws them flat until you build it again.

tools.name: proposals_create

tools.description: If operation fields appear as unknown, call schema with the operation name. Propose a change against a fresh revision from presentations_get or slides_get. The app tries the operations, each with exactly the keys the schema gives it, without writing them; nothing is written until proposals_accept. Use stable slide/object/step ids from slides_get; it also discovers parameter targets, current values and interpolation. Initial values, timed keyframes and cues use the shared agent contract. New keyframe and cue ids must be fresh within a step; reusing an id replaces its whole record. A null key value clears an optional property to its text-style/default, while a null updateStep entry deletes that keyframe or cue. insertSlide takes an optional slideId of your choosing and objects to seed the new slide. insertObject takes an optional objectId. It can’t name a slide inserted by the same proposal. A proposal its validation refuses is not held: the call fails with validation-failed, and the error's validation holds its errors and warnings; an error with code no-change means everything is already so.
